body:
Reproducing this on current `master` using the provided MRP:

```
Godot v4.5.beta (6c9aa4c7d)
- EndeavourOS #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu, 28 Aug 2025 19:49:53 +0000 on Wayland
- X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor
- Vulkan (Forward+)
- dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti (nvidia; 580.76.05)
- 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-12900KF (24 threads)
- 31.16 GiB memory
```

The actual behaviour here seems a bit more involved:
- Setting the desired values in Editor before playing yields the expected results.
- Changing the layer masks (both mesh layers and shadow caster mask) at runtime (via the "Remote" inspector) does not seem to properly update the `OmniLight` culling in either direction until the actual light `Cull Mask` is modified.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1229c43a-26af-4183-af9e-f4a773ad68e5

More than just a performance concern, as can be seen in this recording it's actually possible to get erroneous cached shadowmaps for moving objects.

It looks like we're getting some different results between 4.4.1 and master due to commit: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/305216f55819c3385b3fc3941d0715abd386b74f

The following code has been added to _instance_pair in renderer_scene_cull.cpp

```
		if (!(light->cull_mask & A->layer_mask)) {
			// Early return if the object's layer mask doesn't match the light's cull mask.
			return;
		}
```

I suspect before this was added you probably wouldn't get the stuck shadows as it would be redrawing every frame anyway.

It looks like this change would affect the reproducibility of the originally reported issue using the MRP, however as it still doesn't appear to check the shadow caster mask in the latest code 2 lines later, so changing the settings a bit should still demonstrate the original issue.

```
		if (geom->can_cast_shadows) {
			light->make_shadow_dirty();
		}
```


1. Set the camera to show layer 1 & 2
2. Set box 1 to only layer 1, not rotating
3. Set box 2 to only layer 2, rotating
4. Set omni-light:
5. Cull mask to 1+2
6. Shadow mask to 1 only
7. Layers to 1+2

Looking at the visual profier I'd expect to see it redrawing the shadows every frame even though the only moving object isn't in the shadow mask of light. I'm using this in my project to have the player character only cast shadows for "main" lights to reduce the cost. Other lights still need dynamic shadows enabled for "static" geo as it can be built by the player so can't be pre-baked.

As an aside, I suspect the change in the code could affect some projects. Previously it was possible to have an object unlit by a specific light by excluding it from the light cull mask, but still cast a shadow for that light provided it was in both the camera's cull mask and the shadow mask of the light.

This code change looks like that would no longer cast shadows (or at least not flag them dirty in instance pairing, which could result in wonky results if update regions aren't applying the same logic). Possibly a niche requirement but worth considering when this gets looked at.

I guess I should bite the bullet and build a copy of latest to run these tests on too.

Nice catch! Will link the relevant PR here too: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102399

I might play around with that a bit and see if it's as easy as just adding some extra checks for the shadow-caster mask as well.
